title: Isaiah 29 — Woe to Ariel: the sealed scroll and the reversal of the deaf and the blind

verdicts.reasoning: hôy ʾărîʾēl ʾărîʾēl qiryaṯ ḥānāh ḏāwiḏ ... ḥaggîm yinqōp̄û: 'Woe' for hôy and transliterated 'Ariel' (ASV/NRSV/NJPS) exact; 'let the feasts go round' exact.
wahăṣîqôṯî laʾărîʾēl ... wᵉhāyᵉṯāh lî kaʾărîʾēl: repeating 'Ariel' keeps the altar-hearth pun; exact.
wᵉḥānîṯî ḵaddûr ʿālāyiḵ: MT 'all around' kept; LXX kᵉḏāwiḏ, adopted by NRSV, reported. muṣṣāḇ 'posted troops' (ASV). Defensible under the MT policy.

Disputed vs ASV 'one that hath a familiar spirit'. kᵉʾôḇ mēʾereṣ qôlēḵ: ʾôḇ is the spirit of a dead person called up from the ground; 'a ghost' (NRSV/NJPS) is exact and avoids a misleading archaism. tiššaḥ 'come low', tᵉṣap̄ṣēp̄ 'whisper' fine.
kᵉʾāḇāq daq hămôn zārāyiḵ ... lᵉp̄eṯaʿ piṯʾōm: exact.
mēʿim YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ tippāqēḏ: neutral 'visited' (ASV) leaves the judgment/rescue ambiguity of the Niphal open, as the note explains. Defensible.
kaḥălôm ḥăzôn lāylāh hămôn kol-haggôyim haṣṣōḇᵉʾîm ʿal-ʾărîʾēl: exact.
kaʾăšer yaḥălōm hārāʿēḇ wᵉhinnēh ʾôḵēl wᵉhēqîṣ wᵉrêqāh napšô ...: exact.

hiṯmahmᵉhû ûṯᵉmāhû hištaʿašʿû wāšōʿû: MT 'Tarry' (√mhh) kept, and šʿʿ rendered 'blind yourselves and be blind'. Non-blocking: this is the same root as 32:3 'smeared over' and 6:10; a cross-reference in the 32:3 note would be enough.
kî-nāsaḵ ʿălêḵem YHWH rûaḥ tardēmāh ...: 'a spirit of deep sleep' under central tardemah; the glosses 'the prophets … the seers' are translated, with their likely secondary status noted. Exact.

citations: Tov, Textual Criticism of the Hebrew Bible (3rd ed., 2012), on Ketiv/Qere
verdicts.reasoning: Ketiv/Qere verified: K hspr / Q sēp̄er. 'a sealed scroll' for a rolled, sealed document (Jer 32:10-14) is exact; literal 'one who knows writing'. Disputed vs ASV 'book … learned'; defensible.

Canon-cited. wᵉnittan hassēp̄er ʿal ʾăšer lōʾ-yāḏaʿ sēp̄er ...: 'the scroll', 'does not know writing' literal. Lens check: 'scroll' names the object and does not hint at which writing (the rationale says so explicitly); the reception note accurately reports TBWTT 3.
wayyōʾmer ʾăḏōnāy ... miṣwaṯ ʾănāšîm mᵉlummāḏāh: standalone 'the Lord' kept distinct from YHWH; 'learned by rote' exact.
hinnî yôsip̄ lᵉhap̄lîʾ ... hap̄lēʾ wāp̄eleʾ: 'wonder upon wonder' exact.
hôy hammaʿămîqîm mēYHWH lastir ʿēṣāh: exact.
hap̄ḵᵉḵem ʾim-kᵉḥōmer hayyōṣēr yēḥāšēḇ ... wᵉyēṣer ʾāmar lᵉyôṣᵉrô: 'Your perversity!', articular 'the potter', suffixed 'the one who formed it'; faithful to the potter ruling.
wᵉšāḇ lᵉḇānôn lakkarmel: exact.
wᵉšāmᵉʿû ... haḥērᵉšîm diḇrê-sēp̄er: 'the words of a scroll' keeps the link to vv. 11-12; exact.
wᵉyāsᵉp̄û ʿănāwîm baYHWH śimḥāh wᵉʾeḇyônê ʾāḏām: exact.
Canon-cited. kî-ʾāp̄ēs ʿārîṣ wᵉḵālāh lēṣ ... šōqᵉḏê ʾāwen: exact. Lens check: courtroom sense kept; the canon's Pisces/Aquarius application is in a labelled note.
Canon-cited. maḥăṭîʾê ʾāḏām bᵉḏāḇār ... wayyaṭṭû ḇattōhû ṣaddîq: forensic sense rendered exactly; 'emptiness' (ASV 'a thing of nought'). Defensible.
kōh-ʾāmar YHWH ʾel-bêṯ yaʿăqōḇ ʾăšer pāḏāh ʾeṯ-ʾaḇrāhām: the relative is attached to YHWH (ASV/NRSV); exact.
kî ḇirʾōṯô yᵉlāḏāyw maʿăśēh yāḏay ... ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl yaʿărîṣû: exact; construct epithet 'the God of Israel'.
wᵉyāḏᵉʿû ṯōʿê-rûaḥ bînāh: human rûaḥ 'in spirit'; exact.

citations: Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 40–55 (AB 19A, 2002), ad loc. (45:18 “a formless waste”)
glossaryReview.reasoning: direct verified: the range concrete 'waste' → abstract 'nothingness' is in both lexica; 'emptiness' for the worthlessness sites, adverbial 'in vain' at 45:19 and concrete 'a wasteland' at 45:18 (opposed to lā-šeḇeṯ, echoing the corpus's Gen 1:2 'wasteland and emptiness') are each the standard sense in context. Declining 'chaos' at 45:18 removes a mythic overtone the antithesis does not need.

direct verified: 'the potter' for articular hay-yôṣēr (29:16) and verbal 'the one who formed him / forms it' for suffixed yōṣᵉrô (29:16b; 45:9, 11) is a literal, consistent rule that keeps yāṣar visible against bārāʾ/ʿāśāh; NRSV's 'potter' at 45:9b is recorded as the idiomatic alternative.

paragraphs.text: ה֚וֹי אֲרִיאֵ֣ל אֲרִיאֵ֔ל קִרְיַ֖ת חָנָ֣ה דָוִ֑ד סְפ֥וּ שָׁנָ֛ה עַל־שָׁנָ֖ה חַגִּ֥ים יִנְקֹֽפוּ׃

i18n.en: Woe, Ariel, Ariel, the city where David encamped! Add year to year; let the feasts go round.
i18n.he: ה֚וֹי אֲרִיאֵ֣ל אֲרִיאֵ֔ל קִרְיַ֖ת חָנָ֣ה דָוִ֑ד סְפ֥וּ שָׁנָ֛ה עַל־שָׁנָ֖ה חַגִּ֥ים יִנְקֹֽפוּ׃

notes.official: *ʾărîʾēl* is a cipher-name for Jerusalem, “the city where David encamped.” Ezek 43:15–16 uses the same word for the altar-hearth of the Temple, and v. 2 plays on that sense: the city “shall be to me like an Ariel,” that is, a hearth where fire burns. A second explanation derives the name from “lion of El.” The line transliterates “Ariel” at vv. 1, 2 and 7 with ASV, NRSV and NJPS, so that the name and the pun on it remain one word (overlay `ariel-ob-isaiah-29`; Wildberger, *Isaiah 28–39*, 2002). *hôy* is “Woe” (ASV “Ho”), the opening cry of a funeral lament.

paragraphs.text: וַהֲצִיק֖וֹתִי לַֽאֲרִיאֵ֑ל וְהָיְתָ֤ה תַֽאֲנִיָּה֙ וַֽאֲנִיָּ֔ה וְהָ֥יְתָה לִּ֖י כַּאֲרִיאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: Then I will distress Ariel, and there shall be moaning and lamentation, and she shall be to me like an Ariel.
i18n.he: וַהֲצִיק֖וֹתִי לַֽאֲרִיאֵ֑ל וְהָיְתָ֤ה תַֽאֲנִיָּה֙ וַֽאֲנִיָּ֔ה וְהָ֥יְתָה לִּ֖י כַּאֲרִיאֵֽל׃

notes.official: “She shall be to me like an Ariel”: the city named Ariel will become an *ʾărîʾēl*, an altar-hearth, the place of burning (see v. 1). The pun works only if the same word stands in both places, so the line repeats the name.

paragraphs.text: וְחָנִ֥יתִי כַדּ֖וּר עָלָ֑יִךְ וְצַרְתִּ֤י עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ מֻצָּ֔ב וַהֲקִֽימֹתִ֥י עָלַ֖יִךְ מְצֻרֹֽת׃

i18n.en: And I will encamp against you all around, and lay siege against you with posted troops, and raise siege works against you.
i18n.he: וְחָנִ֥יתִי כַדּ֖וּר עָלָ֑יִךְ וְצַרְתִּ֤י עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ מֻצָּ֔ב וַהֲקִֽימֹתִ֥י עָלַ֖יִךְ מְצֻרֹֽת׃

notes.official: MT *kad-dûr* is “like a circle,” that is, “all around” (ASV “round about”). The LXX read *kᵉḏāwiḏ* “like David” (*hōs Dauid*), which echoes v. 1 (“I will encamp against you as David did”), and NRSV adopts it. The line keeps MT. *muṣṣāḇ* is “posted troops” (ASV) or a siege post or palisade.

paragraphs.text: וְשָׁפַלְתְּ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ תְּדַבֵּ֔רִי וּמֵֽעָפָ֖ר תִּשַּׁ֣ח אִמְרָתֵ֑ךְ וְֽ֠הָיָה כְּא֤וֹב מֵאֶ֙רֶץ֙ קוֹלֵ֔ךְ וּמֵעָפָ֖ר אִמְרָתֵ֥ךְ תְּצַפְצֵֽף׃

i18n.en: And you shall be brought low; from the ground you will speak, and from the dust your speech will come low; and your voice will be like that of a ghost from the ground, and from the dust your speech will whisper.
i18n.he: וְשָׁפַלְתְּ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ תְּדַבֵּ֔רִי וּמֵֽעָפָ֖ר תִּשַּׁ֣ח אִמְרָתֵ֑ךְ וְֽ֠הָיָה כְּא֤וֹב מֵאֶ֙רֶץ֙ קוֹלֵ֔ךְ וּמֵעָפָ֖ר אִמְרָתֵ֥ךְ תְּצַפְצֵֽף׃

notes.official: *kᵉʾôḇ mē-ʾereṣ qôlēḵ* “your voice shall be like that of a ghost from the ground.” *ʾôḇ* is the spirit of a dead person called up by a medium, or the medium who calls it (1 Sam 28:7–8; Lev 19:31; Isa 8:19, where such voices “chirp and mutter”). The humbled city speaks in the faint, twittering voice of the dead from under the earth. ASV has “one that hath a familiar spirit”; the line follows NRSV and NJPS “a ghost,” because “familiar spirit” now suggests a witch’s companion animal (overlay `ariel-ob-isaiah-29`).

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֛ה כְּאָבָ֥ק דַּ֖ק הֲמ֣וֹן זָרָ֑יִךְ וּכְמֹ֤ץ עֹבֵר֙ הֲמ֣וֹן עָֽרִיצִ֔ים וְהָיָ֖ה לְפֶ֥תַע פִּתְאֹֽם׃

i18n.en: But the multitude of your foes shall be like fine dust, and the multitude of the ruthless like chaff that passes away; and it shall be in an instant, suddenly.
i18n.he: וְהָיָ֛ה כְּאָבָ֥ק דַּ֖ק הֲמ֣וֹן זָרָ֑יִךְ וּכְמֹ֤ץ עֹבֵר֙ הֲמ֣וֹן עָֽרִיצִ֔ים וְהָיָ֖ה לְפֶ֥תַע פִּתְאֹֽם׃

paragraphs.text: מֵעִ֨ם יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ תִּפָּקֵ֔ד בְּרַ֥עַם וּבְרַ֖עַשׁ וְק֣וֹל גָּד֑וֹל סוּפָה֙ וּסְעָרָ֔ה וְלַ֖הַב אֵ֥שׁ אוֹכֵלָֽה׃

i18n.en: From YHWH of hosts she will be visited with thunder and with earthquake and great noise, with whirlwind and tempest and the flame of a devouring fire.
i18n.he: מֵעִ֨ם יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ תִּפָּקֵ֔ד בְּרַ֥עַם וּבְרַ֖עַשׁ וְק֣וֹל גָּד֑וֹל סוּפָה֙ וּסְעָרָ֔ה וְלַ֖הַב אֵ֥שׁ אוֹכֵלָֽה׃

notes.official: *tippāqēḏ* “she will be visited” (Niphal of *pqd*) is ambiguous. *pqd* can mean visitation in judgment (so the overlay renders 24:22 “punished”) or in rescue. Here the besieging nations are scattered like dust and vanish like a dream (vv. 5, 7–8), which suggests rescue (NJPS “she shall be remembered”). The storm-theophany (thunder, earthquake, whirlwind, fire) is the standard imagery of YHWH’s intervention. The line keeps the neutral “visited” (ASV), which leaves both senses open.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֗ה כַּֽחֲלוֹם֙ חֲז֣וֹן לַ֔יְלָה הֲמוֹן֙ כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם הַצֹּבְאִ֖ים עַל־אֲרִיאֵ֑ל וְכָל־צֹבֶ֙יהָ֙ וּמְצֹ֣דָתָ֔הּ וְהַמְּצִיקִ֖ים לָֽהּ׃

i18n.en: And like a dream, a vision of the night, shall be the multitude of all the nations that fight against Ariel, all that fight against her and her stronghold and that distress her.
i18n.he: וְהָיָ֗ה כַּֽחֲלוֹם֙ חֲז֣וֹן לַ֔יְלָה הֲמוֹן֙ כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם הַצֹּבְאִ֖ים עַל־אֲרִיאֵ֑ל וְכָל־צֹבֶ֙יהָ֙ וּמְצֹ֣דָתָ֔הּ וְהַמְּצִיקִ֖ים לָֽהּ׃

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֡ה כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ יַחֲלֹ֨ם הָרָעֵ֜ב וְהִנֵּ֣ה אוֹכֵ֗ל וְהֵקִיץ֮ וְרֵיקָ֣ה נַפְשׁוֹ֒ וְכַאֲשֶׁ֨ר יַחֲלֹ֤ם הַצָּמֵא֙ וְהִנֵּ֣ה שֹׁתֶ֔ה וְהֵקִיץ֙ וְהִנֵּ֣ה עָיֵ֔ף וְנַפְשׁ֖וֹ שׁוֹקֵקָ֑ה כֵּ֣ן יִֽהְיֶ֗ה הֲמוֹן֙ כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם הַצֹּבְאִ֖ים עַל־הַ֥ר צִיּֽוֹן׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And it shall be as when a hungry man dreams, and behold, he is eating, but he awakes and his soul is empty; or as when a thirsty man dreams, and behold, he is drinking, but he awakes, and behold, he is faint and his soul is craving: so shall the multitude of all the nations be that fight against Mount Zion.
i18n.he: וְהָיָ֡ה כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ יַחֲלֹ֨ם הָרָעֵ֜ב וְהִנֵּ֣ה אוֹכֵ֗ל וְהֵקִיץ֮ וְרֵיקָ֣ה נַפְשׁוֹ֒ וְכַאֲשֶׁ֨ר יַחֲלֹ֤ם הַצָּמֵא֙ וְהִנֵּ֣ה שֹׁתֶ֔ה וְהֵקִיץ֙ וְהִנֵּ֣ה עָיֵ֔ף וְנַפְשׁ֖וֹ שׁוֹקֵקָ֑ה כֵּ֣ן יִֽהְיֶ֗ה הֲמוֹן֙ כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם הַצֹּבְאִ֖ים עַל־הַ֥ר צִיּֽוֹן׃ (ס)

paragraphs.text: הִתְמַהְמְה֣וּ וּתְמָ֔הוּ הִשְׁתַּֽעַשְׁע֖וּ וָשֹׁ֑עוּ שָֽׁכְר֣וּ וְלֹא־יַ֔יִן נָע֖וּ וְלֹ֥א שֵׁכָֽר׃

i18n.en: Tarry and be astounded; blind yourselves and be blind! They are drunk, but not with wine; they stagger, but not with strong drink.
i18n.he: הִתְמַהְמְה֣וּ וּתְמָ֔הוּ הִשְׁתַּֽעַשְׁע֖וּ וָשֹׁ֑עוּ שָֽׁכְר֣וּ וְלֹא־יַ֔יִן נָע֖וּ וְלֹ֥א שֵׁכָֽר׃

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־נָסַ֨ךְ עֲלֵיכֶ֤ם יְהוָה֙ ר֣וּחַ תַּרְדֵּמָ֔ה וַיְעַצֵּ֖ם אֶת־עֵֽינֵיכֶ֑ם אֶת־הַנְּבִיאִ֛ים וְאֶת־רָאשֵׁיכֶ֥ם הַחֹזִ֖ים כִּסָּֽה׃

i18n.en: For YHWH has poured out upon you a spirit of deep sleep, and has closed your eyes, the prophets, and has covered your heads, the seers.
i18n.he: כִּֽי־נָסַ֨ךְ עֲלֵיכֶ֤ם יְהוָה֙ ר֣וּחַ תַּרְדֵּמָ֔ה וַיְעַצֵּ֖ם אֶת־עֵֽינֵיכֶ֑ם אֶת־הַנְּבִיאִ֛ים וְאֶת־רָאשֵׁיכֶ֥ם הַחֹזִ֖ים כִּסָּֽה׃

notes.official: *rûaḥ tardēmāh* “a spirit of deep sleep”: *tardēmāh* is “deep sleep” under the central `tardemah-divine-induced-deep-sleep` entry, the sleep YHWH causes (Gen 2:21; 15:12). The glosses “the prophets” and “the seers,” set in apposition to “your eyes” and “your heads,” are often taken as later explanatory additions (Wildberger); they are in MT and are translated.

paragraphs.text: וַתְּהִ֨י לָכֶ֜ם חָז֣וּת הַכֹּ֗ל כְּדִבְרֵי֮ הַסֵּ֣פֶר הֶֽחָתוּם֒ אֲשֶֽׁר־יִתְּנ֣וּ אֹת֗וֹ אֶל־יוֹדֵ֥עַ הספר [סֵ֛פֶר] לֵאמֹ֖ר קְרָ֣א נָא־זֶ֑ה וְאָמַר֙ לֹ֣א אוּכַ֔ל כִּ֥י חָת֖וּם הֽוּא׃

i18n.en: And the vision of all this has become for you like the words of a sealed scroll, which they give to one who knows writing, saying, “Read this, please,” and he says, “I cannot, for it is sealed.”
i18n.he: וַתְּהִ֨י לָכֶ֜ם חָז֣וּת הַכֹּ֗ל כְּדִבְרֵי֮ הַסֵּ֣פֶר הֶֽחָתוּם֒ אֲשֶֽׁר־יִתְּנ֣וּ אֹת֗וֹ אֶל־יוֹדֵ֥עַ הספר [סֵ֛פֶר] לֵאמֹ֖ר קְרָ֣א נָא־זֶ֑ה וְאָמַר֙ לֹ֣א אוּכַ֔ל כִּ֥י חָת֖וּם הֽוּא׃

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere. In *yôḏēaʿ sēp̄er*, “one who knows writing,” the consonantal text has the article (הספר) and the Masoretes read *sēp̄er* without it, matching v. 12; the qere is read (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). *sēp̄er* is any written document. A “sealed” *sēp̄er* is a rolled document closed with a seal impression, like the deed of Jer 32:10–14. The line has “a sealed scroll” in place of ASV’s “a book,” and keeps the idiom *yôḏēaʿ sēp̄er* literally, “one who knows writing,” in place of ASV’s “learned” (overlay `sefer-sealed-scroll-isaiah-29`).

paragraphs.text: וְנִתַּ֣ן הַסֵּ֗פֶר עַל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־יָדַ֥ע סֵ֛פֶר לֵאמֹ֖ר קְרָ֣א נָא־זֶ֑ה וְאָמַ֕ר לֹ֥א יָדַ֖עְתִּי סֵֽפֶר׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And the scroll is given to one who does not know writing, saying, “Read this, please,” and he says, “I do not know writing.”
i18n.he: וְנִתַּ֣ן הַסֵּ֗פֶר עַל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־יָדַ֥ע סֵ֛פֶר לֵאמֹ֖ר קְרָ֣א נָא־זֶ֑ה וְאָמַ֕ר לֹ֥א יָדַ֖עְתִּי סֵֽפֶר׃ (ס)

notes.official:
The second half of the parable: the scroll is now given to one who cannot read. Between the literate man, who cannot open it, and the illiterate, who cannot read it, the vision stays closed to everyone. The idiom “one who does not know writing” is kept literally (see v. 11).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) quotes v. 12 (“the writing is delivered to one that is not learned … and he saith, I am not learned”). It reads the verse as a picture of humanity holding the truth for a long time without being able to “read” it until it was scientifically advanced enough. The line keeps the physical object, “the scroll,” and the literal idiom, and does not identify the writing.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲדֹנָ֗י יַ֚עַן כִּ֤י נִגַּשׁ֙ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה בְּפִ֤יו וּבִשְׂפָתָיו֙ כִּבְּד֔וּנִי וְלִבּ֖וֹ רִחַ֣ק מִמֶּ֑נִּי וַתְּהִ֤י יִרְאָתָם֙ אֹתִ֔י מִצְוַ֥ת אֲנָשִׁ֖ים מְלֻמָּדָֽה׃

i18n.en: And the Lord said: “Because this people draws near with its mouth and honors me with its lips, but has removed its heart far from me, and their fear of me is a commandment of men learned by rote,
i18n.he: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲדֹנָ֗י יַ֚עַן כִּ֤י נִגַּשׁ֙ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה בְּפִ֤יו וּבִשְׂפָתָיו֙ כִּבְּד֔וּנִי וְלִבּ֖וֹ רִחַ֣ק מִמֶּ֑נִּי וַתְּהִ֤י יִרְאָתָם֙ אֹתִ֔י מִצְוַ֥ת אֲנָשִׁ֖ים מְלֻמָּדָֽה׃

notes.official: *wayyōʾmer ʾăḏōnāy* “And the Lord said”: the standalone title *ʾăḏōnāy* is “the Lord” under the overlay entry written for Isa 6, kept distinct from YHWH. *miṣwaṯ ʾănāšîm mᵉlummāḏāh* “a commandment of men learned by rote” is quoted in the LXX form at Mark 7:6–7 and Matt 15:8–9.

paragraphs.text: לָכֵ֗ן הִנְנִ֥י יוֹסִ֛ף לְהַפְלִ֥יא אֶת־הָֽעָם־הַזֶּ֖ה הַפְלֵ֣א וָפֶ֑לֶא וְאָֽבְדָה֙ חָכְמַ֣ת חֲכָמָ֔יו וּבִינַ֥ת נְבֹנָ֖יו תִּסְתַּתָּֽר׃ (ס)

i18n.en: therefore, behold, I will again do a wonder with this people, wonder upon wonder; and the wisdom of its wise men shall perish, and the understanding of its discerning men shall be hidden.”
i18n.he: לָכֵ֗ן הִנְנִ֥י יוֹסִ֛ף לְהַפְלִ֥יא אֶת־הָֽעָם־הַזֶּ֖ה הַפְלֵ֣א וָפֶ֑לֶא וְאָֽבְדָה֙ חָכְמַ֣ת חֲכָמָ֔יו וּבִינַ֥ת נְבֹנָ֖יו תִּסְתַּתָּֽר׃ (ס)

paragraphs.text: ה֛וֹי הַמַּעֲמִיקִ֥ים מֵֽיהוָ֖ה לַסְתִּ֣ר עֵצָ֑ה וְהָיָ֤ה בְמַחְשָׁךְ֙ מַֽעֲשֵׂיהֶ֔ם וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ מִ֥י רֹאֵ֖נוּ וּמִ֥י יוֹדְעֵֽנוּ׃

i18n.en: Woe to those who hide their counsel deep from YHWH, whose deeds are in the dark, and who say, “Who sees us? And who knows us?”
i18n.he: ה֛וֹי הַמַּעֲמִיקִ֥ים מֵֽיהוָ֖ה לַסְתִּ֣ר עֵצָ֑ה וְהָיָ֤ה בְמַחְשָׁךְ֙ מַֽעֲשֵׂיהֶ֔ם וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ מִ֥י רֹאֵ֖נוּ וּמִ֥י יוֹדְעֵֽנוּ׃

paragraphs.text: הַ֨פְכְּכֶ֔ם אִם־כְּחֹ֥מֶר הַיֹּצֵ֖ר יֵֽחָשֵׁ֑ב כִּֽי־יֹאמַ֨ר מַעֲשֶׂ֤ה לְעֹשֵׂ֙הוּ֙ לֹ֣א עָשָׂ֔נִי וְיֵ֛צֶר אָמַ֥ר לְיוֹצְר֖וֹ לֹ֥א הֵבִֽין׃

i18n.en: Your perversity! Shall the potter be regarded as the clay, that the thing made should say of its maker, “He did not make me,” and the thing formed say of the one who formed it, “He has no understanding”?
i18n.he: הַ֨פְכְּכֶ֔ם אִם־כְּחֹ֥מֶר הַיֹּצֵ֖ר יֵֽחָשֵׁ֑ב כִּֽי־יֹאמַ֨ר מַעֲשֶׂ֤ה לְעֹשֵׂ֙הוּ֙ לֹ֣א עָשָׂ֔נִי וְיֵ֛צֶר אָמַ֥ר לְיוֹצְר֖וֹ לֹ֥א הֵבִֽין׃

notes.official: *hăp̄ākᵉḵem* “your perversity!” (literally “your turning upside down”) is an exclamation. The line keeps the substantive *hay-yôṣēr* as “the potter” (ASV, NRSV, NJPS), because here the craftsman is named over against the clay. The suffixed participle *yōṣᵉrô* in the next clause (“of the one who formed it”) keeps the verbal force of *yāṣar* “form,” and *ʿōśēhû* is “its maker” (central `asah`). One ruling covers all of Isaiah’s clay passages (29:16; 45:9; 64:7): “the potter” for the free-standing noun, “the one who formed him/it” for the suffixed participle (overlay `yotser-potter-clay-image-isaiah`; central `yatsar`).

paragraphs.text: הֲלוֹא־עוֹד֙ מְעַ֣ט מִזְעָ֔ר וְשָׁ֥ב לְבָנ֖וֹן לַכַּרְמֶ֑ל וְהַכַּרְמֶ֖ל לַיַּ֥עַר יֵחָשֵֽׁב׃

i18n.en: Is it not yet a very little while until Lebanon is turned into a fruitful field, and the fruitful field is regarded as a forest?
i18n.he: הֲלוֹא־עוֹד֙ מְעַ֣ט מִזְעָ֔ר וְשָׁ֥ב לְבָנ֖וֹן לַכַּרְמֶ֑ל וְהַכַּרְמֶ֖ל לַיַּ֥עַר יֵחָשֵֽׁב׃

paragraphs.text: וְשָׁמְע֧וּ בַיּוֹם־הַה֛וּא הַחֵרְשִׁ֖ים דִּבְרֵי־סֵ֑פֶר וּמֵאֹ֣פֶל וּמֵחֹ֔שֶׁךְ עֵינֵ֥י עִוְרִ֖ים תִּרְאֶֽינָה׃

i18n.en: And in that day the deaf shall hear the words of a scroll, and out of gloom and out of darkness the eyes of the blind shall see.
i18n.he: וְשָׁמְע֧וּ בַיּוֹם־הַה֛וּא הַחֵרְשִׁ֖ים דִּבְרֵי־סֵ֑פֶר וּמֵאֹ֣פֶל וּמֵחֹ֔שֶׁךְ עֵינֵ֥י עִוְרִ֖ים תִּרְאֶֽינָה׃

notes.official: “The words of a scroll” takes up the sealed scroll of vv. 11–12 (see the note at v. 11). On the day of reversal the deaf hear what was written and the blind see, and the closed vision of vv. 9–12 is opened.

paragraphs.text: וְיָסְפ֧וּ עֲנָוִ֛ים בַּֽיהוָ֖ה שִׂמְחָ֑ה וְאֶבְיוֹנֵ֣י אָדָ֔ם בִּקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יָגִֽילוּ׃

i18n.en: And the meek shall increase their joy in YHWH, and the poorest of humankind shall rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.
i18n.he: וְיָסְפ֧וּ עֲנָוִ֛ים בַּֽיהוָ֖ה שִׂמְחָ֑ה וְאֶבְיוֹנֵ֣י אָדָ֔ם בִּקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יָגִֽילוּ׃

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־אָפֵ֥ס עָרִ֖יץ וְכָ֣לָה לֵ֑ץ וְנִכְרְת֖וּ כָּל־שֹׁ֥קְדֵי אָֽוֶן׃

i18n.en: For the ruthless one is brought to nothing, and the scoffer is finished, and all who watch for iniquity are cut off —
i18n.he: כִּֽי־אָפֵ֥ס עָרִ֖יץ וְכָ֣לָה לֵ֑ץ וְנִכְרְת֖וּ כָּל־שֹׁ֥קְדֵי אָֽוֶן׃

notes.official: **Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 5) quotes vv. 20–21 and applies them to those who teach original sin and “lay snares for him who will spread the truth” at the passage from the age of Pisces into Aquarius. In the Hebrew the verses describe corrupt litigants at the city gate, and the line renders them so. *ʿārîṣ* is “the ruthless one,” *lēṣ* “the scoffer,” and *šōqᵉḏê ʾāwen* “all who watch for iniquity.”

paragraphs.text: מַחֲטִיאֵ֤י אָדָם֙ בְּדָבָ֔ר וְלַמּוֹכִ֥יחַ בַּשַּׁ֖עַר יְקֹשׁ֑וּן וַיַּטּ֥וּ בַתֹּ֖הוּ צַדִּֽיק׃ (ס)

i18n.en: those who make a man an offender by a word, and lay a snare for the one who reproves in the gate, and turn aside the righteous with emptiness.
i18n.he: מַחֲטִיאֵ֤י אָדָם֙ בְּדָבָ֔ר וְלַמּוֹכִ֥יחַ בַּשַּׁ֖עַר יְקֹשׁ֑וּן וַיַּטּ֥וּ בַתֹּ֖הוּ צַדִּֽיק׃ (ס)

notes.official: The three clauses describe abuse of the court at the city gate. *maḥăṭîʾê ʾāḏām bᵉḏāḇār* is “those who make a man an offender by a word,” that is, who convict by false testimony. *wᵉlam-môḵîaḥ baš-šaʿar yᵉqōšûn* is “lay a snare for the one who reproves in the gate,” the honest witness or arbiter. *wayyaṭṭû ḇat-tōhû ṣaddîq* is “turn aside the righteous with emptiness,” with groundless pleas (NRSV “with empty pleas”; ASV “with a thing of nought”). *tōhû* is rendered “emptiness” here as in its other “nothingness” uses (40:17, 23; 44:9). The “chaos” of the overlay entry for 24:10 would not fit a court idiom (overlay `tohu-bare-emptiness-wasteland-isaiah`).

paragraphs.text: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּדָ֖ה אֶת־אַבְרָהָ֑ם לֹֽא־עַתָּ֤ה יֵבוֹשׁ֙ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וְלֹ֥א עַתָּ֖ה פָּנָ֥יו יֶחֱוָֽרוּ׃

i18n.en: Therefore thus says YHWH, who redeemed Abraham, concerning the house of Jacob: Jacob shall not now be ashamed, nor shall his face now grow pale.
i18n.he: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּדָ֖ה אֶת־אַבְרָהָ֑ם לֹֽא־עַתָּ֤ה יֵבוֹשׁ֙ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וְלֹ֥א עַתָּ֖ה פָּנָ֥יו יֶחֱוָֽרוּ׃

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י בִ֠רְאֹתוֹ יְלָדָ֞יו מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָדַ֛י בְּקִרְבּ֖וֹ יַקְדִּ֣ישֽׁוּ שְׁמִ֑י וְהִקְדִּ֙ישׁוּ֙ אֶת־קְד֣וֹשׁ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וְאֶת־אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יַעֲרִֽיצוּ׃

i18n.en: For when he sees his children, the work of my hands, in his midst, they will sanctify my name; they will sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and will stand in awe of the God of Israel.
i18n.he: כִּ֣י בִ֠רְאֹתוֹ יְלָדָ֞יו מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָדַ֛י בְּקִרְבּ֖וֹ יַקְדִּ֣ישֽׁוּ שְׁמִ֑י וְהִקְדִּ֙ישׁוּ֙ אֶת־קְד֣וֹשׁ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וְאֶת־אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יַעֲרִֽיצוּ׃

notes.official: *ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl* is “the God of Israel” under the overlay construct-epithet pattern. *yalāḏāyw maʿăśēh yāḏay* “his children, the work of my hands” is MT; some take “the work of my hands” as a gloss, but it is translated.

paragraphs.text: וְיָדְע֥וּ תֹֽעֵי־ר֖וּחַ בִּינָ֑ה וְרוֹגְנִ֖ים יִלְמְדוּ־לֶֽקַח׃

i18n.en: And those who err in spirit will come to understanding, and those who murmur will learn instruction.
i18n.he: וְיָדְע֥וּ תֹֽעֵי־ר֖וּחַ בִּינָ֑ה וְרוֹגְנִ֖ים יִלְמְדוּ־לֶֽקַח׃
